To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. front-line workers in long-term care facilities perceive that a high proportion of patients with diabetes are in need of mental health services, and 2. front-line workers are not very confident in their own ability to manage the mental health needs in this population.
front-line diabetes clinicians in long-term care are not very confident in their abilities to meet the mental health needs that they perceive to be present in the patients they serve.

front-line clinicians working in the long-term setting are aware that many patients with diabetes in their care need mental health services but that they are not very confident in their abilities to meet these needs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mental health needs and treatment of patients living with diabetes in the long-term context.
the mental health needs and experiences of patients with diabetes and the confidence of health care workers in their abilities to address such needs in the context of long-term care.
the mental health needs and treatment options for patients living with diabetes in the long-term context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not know what the mental health needs are, or what the barriers and solutions are.
there are a number of important issues to consider in terms of the mental health needs and concerns of patients with diabetes.
there are many mental health needs of long-term patients with diabetes that are unmet and for which front-line staff are ill-prepared.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
front-line clinicians working in long-term care are aware that their patients have mental health needs, but they are uncertain as to how to address those needs.
front-line workers in this setting are not very confident in their ability to manage the mental health needs (psychological/psychiatric) of long-term care facility patients with diabetes.
the mental health needs and the mental health services provided to long-term care residents living with diabetes are not well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
front-line workers in this context are not very confident about their abilities to manage the mental health needs that are common among patients with diabetes.
front-line workers are concerned about the psychological and psychiatric needs of long-term residents living with diabetes.

the needs of patients with mental health issues in the diabetes context are not being adequately addressed in the longterm care setting, and front-line workers are uncertain about what to do to change the situation.
